system_description.narrative_title: Tech-driven militarization and energy surge in a shifting geopolitical order
system_description.narrative_summary: A convergence of rapid commercialisation of advanced weapons, state nuclear and missile activity, and an AI-driven economic boom (centered on South Korea) is reshaping investments, energy infrastructure needs, and regional security alignments. Private capital and tech startups (backed by high-profile investors) are accelerating production of cruise and 'deep strike' missiles even as states (North Korea, Russia, Iran) expand nuclear and missile programs; simultaneously, South Korea's AI expansion is driving massive US investment pledges and pressure to expand energy/nuclear capacity. This is an open system with flows of capital, technology, information, energy, and military capability crossing national boundaries and creating reinforcing feedbacks between economic demand, energy supply choices, and strategic competition.
system_description.scope: Commercialisation and deployment of advanced offensive weapons (mass-producible cruise/deep-strike missiles), state nuclear and missile program developments (North Korea, Iran, Russia), private capital flows into defence and energy tech (Thiel, Andreessen, Gates-backed firms), South Korea's AI-driven economic boom and resulting energy/investment decisions (nuclear, gas, US investments), and technological breakthroughs (fusion) with military applications.
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy markets (LNG, gas, nuclear power, and emerging fusion)
International arms industry and defence supply chains
Global venture-capital and technology investment ecosystem
East Asian regional security architecture (US, South Korea, North Korea, China, Japan)
evidence_headlines: Thiel-backed start-up to mass-produce ‘deep strike’ missiles in Europe and US
North Korea builds new Yongbyon uranium enrichment facility, IAEA says
South Korea's power demand set to soar on AI boom as nation weighs expanding nuclear energy
South Korea nears agreement worth over $100 billion in US investments, WSJ reports
Russia secretly helping Iran develop supersonic cruise missiles
America Leans on Fusion Breakthroughs to Turbocharge Its Nuclear Weapon Arsenal

variables.name: Missile production capacity
variables.description: The aggregate industrial capacity to manufacture offensive cruise and deep‑strike missiles per unit time.

variables.name: Missile arsenal size
variables.description: The total deployed and reserve inventory of offensive missile systems and munitions.

variables.name: Weapon mass‑producibility
variables.description: The ease, cost curve, and standardization level enabling mass production of advanced offensive weapons.

variables.name: Private defense investment rate
variables.description: The rate at which private capital is allocated to defence‑oriented firms and technologies.

variables.name: Public defence spending level
variables.description: The aggregate government budgetary commitment to defence procurement, R&D, and force sustainment.

variables.name: AI‑driven economic output
variables.description: The economic output attributable to AI adoption, measured as value added or GDP contribution from AI‑intensive sectors.

variables.name: AI industry growth rate
variables.description: The tempo of expansion in AI‑related firms, revenues, and employment over time.

variables.name: Electricity demand level
variables.description: The total electrical energy demand across the system per unit time.

variables.name: Energy generation capacity
variables.description: The total installed capacity to generate electricity across all sources.

variables.name: Nuclear generation capacity
variables.description: The installed electrical generation capacity derived from nuclear power facilities.

variables.name: Gas generation capacity
variables.description: The installed electrical generation capacity derived from gas‑fired infrastructure.

variables.name: Fusion technology maturity
variables.description: The technological readiness and commercial maturity of fusion energy and related high‑energy technologies.

variables.name: Cross‑border capital flow rate
variables.description: The net rate of international private and institutional capital movements into technology and energy sectors.

variables.name: Technology diffusion rate
variables.description: The speed at which dual‑use and military‑relevant technologies spread between actors and sectors.

variables.name: Strategic alignment degree
variables.description: The extent and strength of cooperative security alignments and coordinated strategic postures among actors as perceived in the system.

variables.name: Arms‑control and norms strength
variables.description: The robustness and enforcement capacity of formal and informal norms, treaties, and regulatory frameworks governing weapons and related technologies.

catalysts.title: Private missile mass‑production ramp
catalysts.description: Venture‑backed startups begin large‑scale missile manufacturing in the US and Europe, scaling capacity and lowering unit costs.
catalysts.rationale: Thiel‑backed and Andreessen/Thiel‑backed startups open missile factories and pledge mass production (FT; reports 9/9–9/10).

catalysts.title: Private missile production expands into Europe
catalysts.description: US venture‑backed missile firms establish production lines and partnerships in Europe, shifting production geography and capital flows.
catalysts.rationale: FT and other outlets: Thiel‑backed start‑up to mass‑produce deep‑strike missiles in Europe and US (9/9–9/10).

catalysts.title: Russia–Iran missile collaboration intensifies
catalysts.description: Covert and overt assistance accelerates Iran's supersonic/cruise missile programs, expanding production and capabilities.
catalysts.rationale: Reports: Russia secretly helping Iran develop supersonic cruise missiles; Iran producing new missiles (9/8–9/10).

catalysts.title: North Korea enrichment expansion & external links
catalysts.description: Yongbyon enrichment facilities grow while cross‑border infrastructure and diplomatic ties deepen, enabling greater weapons production and external support.
catalysts.rationale: IAEA notes new Yongbyon enrichment facility; bridges and messages show strengthening ties with Russia/China (9/9–9/10).

catalysts.title: South Korea AI boom drives power demand and capital inflows
catalysts.description: Rapid AI adoption spikes electricity needs while triggering large US investments and consideration of expanded nuclear capacity.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: South Korea power demand set to soar on AI boom; nears >$100bn in US investments; $20bn gas plant investment (9/8–9/10).

catalysts.title: US next‑generation fighter program decision
catalysts.description: An imminent procurement/selection announcement for the Navy's next‑gen fighter will set program scale and associated funding trajectories.
catalysts.rationale: Report: US Navy's next‑generation fighter decision to be unveiled soon (9/8).

catalysts.title: Acceleration of fusion tech into defense applications
catalysts.description: Breakthroughs in laser/fusion technologies prompt defense use‑cases (missile defense, weaponized applications), accelerating maturation and diffusion.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Could Laser Fusion Tech Be Used to Shoot Down Missiles...' and 'America Leans on Fusion Breakthroughs...' (9/10).

catalysts.title: Finalization of major US–South Korea investment pact
catalysts.description: Pending agreements worth tens-to-hundreds of billions between US and South Korea reach closure, unlocking capital flows into tech and energy.
catalysts.rationale: Exclusives: South Korea nears agreement on billions and >$100bn in U.S. investments (9/10).

catalysts_scored.rationale: Reports: Russia secretly helping Iran develop supersonic cruise missiles; Iran producing new missiles (9/8–9/10).
